security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, code reads or writes CSR_MSECCFG/CSR_MSECCFGH after checking only that Sm >= 1.12, without also verifying that at least one of Zkr, Smmpm, or Zicfilp is present in the ISA string. On hardware with Sm >= 1.12 but none of those field-defining extensions, the CSR does not exist and access raises an illegal instruction exception.
security_spec.summary: mseccfg/mseccfgh are gated on Sm≥1.12 AND anyOf{Zkr,Smmpm,Zicfilp}; kernel code must not access them based on Sm version alone, or it will trap on hardware lacking field-defining extensions

findings.finding: CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) and CSR_MSECCFGH (0x757) are defined but never accessed via csr_read() or csr_write() anywhere in the kernel. MSECCFG_PMM bit aliases at lines 245-249 are also never used to form CSR accesses. Pointer masking configuration is delegated to SBI FWFT (SBI_EXT_FWFT), not direct CSR manipulation. The vulnerability pattern (csr_read/write CSR_MSECCFG guarded only by Sm >= 1.12) does not match any live code path.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:mseccfg_presence]#It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented. Otherwise, it is reserved.#

findings.finding: MSECCFG_PMM bit aliases are defined (aliased to ENVCFG_PMM) but never used in actual CSR_MSECCFG reads/writes. The Smmpm, Zkr, and Zicfilp ISA extensions are parsed in cpufeature.c but guard no MSECCFG access because none exist.
findings.snippet:
/* mseccfg bits */
#define MSECCFG_PMM			ENVCFG_PMM
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16

spec_citations.excerpt: norm:mseccfg_presence: It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented. Otherwise, it is reserved.
